entities.summary:
Jean-François de la Trémoille (1465-1507) was a French Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a pivotal role in the tumultuous politics of Western Europe during the late Middle Ages.


 As a close advisor to King Louis XII of France, de la Trémoille navigated the treacherous waters of European diplomacy, shaping the course of alliances, wars, and religious conflicts that defined this period. His influence extended across the continent, as he worked tirelessly to promote the interests of France and secure its dominance in a rapidly shifting world.


 De la Trémoille's legacy is marked by his significant contributions to the French monarchy, his role in the Council of Trent, and his steadfast commitment to Catholic orthodoxy. His work laid the groundwork for future generations of French leaders, shaping the country's trajectory for centuries to come.


 The passing of de la Trémoille on June 29, 1507, marked the end of an era, but his impact on European history endured, leaving behind a complex web of alliances, rivalries, and religious divisions that would continue to shape the continent for generations to come.
